issues.description: Monkey-patching genai._api_client.READ_BUFFER_SIZE at import time is wrong-shape
issues.detail: You're reaching into a private attribute (`_api_client`) of a third-party library and mutating module-level state at import time. The author even calls it a 'Temporary hack' in the comment. This is exactly the kind of patch a maintainer refuses on sight. It poisons the global library state for every other consumer in the process, it will silently break when google-genai reorganizes its internals (the underscore is the warning sign), and there is no test that will catch the breakage. Either push the buffer size upstream, use a documented API on the client instance, or stream the bytes properly. Do not land a TODO disguised as code.

issues.description: image.tobytes() with format='RGB' is almost certainly wrong for arbitrary PNG/JPEG output
issues.detail: PIL's `Image.open()` on Nano Banana output will not necessarily give you an RGB-mode image. It could be RGBA, P, L, anything. You then call `image.tobytes()` (raw pixel buffer in whatever mode the image happens to be in) and unconditionally label it `format='RGB'`. If the model returns an RGBA image, the consumer sees 4-byte pixels interpreted as 3-byte RGB and you get garbage on screen. At minimum: `image = image.convert('RGB')` before `tobytes()`, or detect the mode and set the format accordingly. This is a correctness bug, not a style nit.

This diff does three independent things: (1) add image-output handling to GoogleLLMService, (2) bump the default model from gemini-2.0-flash to gemini-2.5-flash, (3) widen the google-* dependency specifiers from `~=` to `>=,<major`. Each of these has a different blast radius and a different reason to revert. The model default change alone is a behavior change for every existing user who didn't pin a model. Split it. Three patches, three commit messages, three revert points.

issues.description: Special-case 'image' substring check is bad taste
issues.detail: `if "image" in self._model_name:` inside `_maybe_unset_thinking_budget` is the kind of stringly-typed special case that bites you in six months when Google ships `gemini-2.5-flash-vision` or `gemini-3-image-pro` or renames the line. Good taste here is asking the model capabilities (does it support thinking budget? does it generate images?), not substring-matching the marketing name. At minimum, lift this into a small capability table or a helper like `_model_supports_thinking_budget()` so the next person adding a model doesn't have to grep for `"image"`.

issues.description: No test coverage for the new image path
issues.detail: A new branch in `_process_context` that opens bytes with PIL, constructs a frame, and pushes it downstream — and the diff contains zero tests. The example script is not a test; it requires a live API key and a transport. At least a unit test that feeds a fake `Part` with `inline_data.data` set to a known PNG/JPEG and asserts the resulting `OutputImageRawFrame` has the right size and format. Without it, the format='RGB' bug above ships unnoticed.

issues.description: Stray blank line added with no purpose
issues.detail: Line 717 adds a blank line after `self._http_options = http_options` for no reason. Diff noise. Drop it.

The docstring says 'A conversational AI bot using Gemini for both LLM, STT and TTS' — fine — but the headline feature of the example is image generation and the file is named `07n-interruptible-gemini-image.py`. Lead with that. Also the copyright header says '2024-2025' on a brand-new file in 2026; either drop the year or get it right.

issues.description: Default model change is a behavior change that deserves a louder note
issues.detail: Bumping the default from `gemini-2.0-flash` to `gemini-2.5-flash` is a real change for every caller relying on the default. The CHANGELOG entry exists but it's a one-liner under 'Changed'. For a default-model bump, callers want to know: cost delta, latency delta, behavior delta. A sentence in the changelog and a line in the docstring of `__init__` is the minimum.

review.summary: Adds image-output handling to GoogleLLMService plus a default-model bump and a dependency widening. The feature itself is small and the right shape conceptually, but two of the lines that actually land have real problems: a private-attribute monkey-patch on the genai client (the author labels it a hack, and it is one), and an `image.tobytes()` with a hardcoded `format='RGB'` that will produce garbage pixels for any non-RGB-mode image the model returns. There are also three logically separate changes squashed into one PR, a stringly-typed `\"image\" in model_name` special case, and zero test coverage for the new branch. NEEDS-WORK: fix the buffer hack and the RGB conversion, split the model-default and dependency changes out, add a unit test for the image-decoding path. Then it lands.
